properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-12, thinking out loud; nothing here is chosen).

His words: "in flo2-connector.github.io/reflow2, we discuss how the hub/project brain works, but I don't think we publish anything about just a simple case of one design by itself. Trying to think how to convey from a single design project perspective, what reflow2 is. Maybe we could talk about the design process through to implementation?"

What the site holds today (fact:the-home-pages-headline-describes-a-hub-and-project-brain-names-both-2026-10-12): the home page opens on "One shared design across all your repositories", which defines a hub. hub.html is "a hub, or project brain". setup.html covers installation only. No page follows one design from the first requirement to working code.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) HIS: walk the design process through to implementation, for one design. The steps: say what it must do, reflow2 asks what is missing, decide and record why, build what the design says, and change it while seeing what the change touches.
(b) Re-centre the HOME page on one design and move "one brain across all your repositories" to hub.html, so the single design comes first and the hub reads as the next step. This changes what exists rather than adding a page.
(c) A new page beside hub.html, "One design", hand-written around a made-up example. The home page links to it the way it links to the hub.
(d) Follow ONE of the Gearheads' repositories (next season's climber) as a single design, from intent to code. This reuses the made-up example the home page already tells.
(e) Show a REAL design going from requirement to code, such as reflow2's own or the calculator's.

These combine; (a) is the story, and (b) to (e) are where it lives and whose example it uses.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-12 — promoted into: the site shows one design by itself before any hub, a made-up example followed from its first requirement into the code and back
properties.rationale:
Counter-arguments and costs, recorded beside the idea, not against it:

1. SETTLED CONSTRAINT: dec:the-sites-setup-pages-are-hand-written-and-its-design-pages-stay-generated (accepted 2026-10-05). A page written for someone without reflow2 is hand-written and told through a made-up example; any page that shows a REAL design's content stays generated from that design. (a), (b), (c) and (d) fit that as hand-written pages. (e) is much larger: it needs a generator that renders a design's thread from requirement to code, and the page then becomes evidence that must stay true to that design. That decision settles HOW a page is written; this question is WHAT story the site tells, so the two are distinct.

2. "THROUGH TO IMPLEMENTATION" STOPS SHORT OF THE VISION. docs/vision.md says "concept to operations", and req:design-and-implementation-stay-coherent-both-ways is accepted. A walkthrough that ends when the code is written reads as a waterfall requirements tool. What sets reflow2 apart is what happens after the code exists: drift between code and design is caught, a change shows what it touches before anyone edits, and test results flow back into the design. If (a) is taken, its last steps would loop back from the code to the design.

3. COST PER RELEASE. Each page is one more page the standing rule (req:every-release-brings-reflow2s-site-up-to-date-with-what-it-ships) has every cut read for content, and one more "Checked against" line. (b) adds no page; (c) adds one; (e) adds a generator to keep working.

4. THE NAME. "Project brain" names both the home page's subject and the hub. Whichever option is taken, one of the two pages probably needs a different name, or a reader cannot tell a single design from a hub. Noted only; not chosen.

5. AUDIENCE, for (a): the single-design case is how most people start. Anthony at work has one project in VS Code through --call. The hub is the second step, so the site currently teaches the advanced case first.
